# Volume 1 — CHAPTER VII. Nell Says Her Prayers

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

At the time Thirza escorted Nell upstairs to bed that evening, she remarked rigidly:
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0000 }

“Now, Nell, I saw yesterday evening that you dropped your garments everywhere across the ground as you undressed. That shows a lack of neatness, and I am unable to permit it whatsoever. The moment you remove each piece of attire, crease it orderly and set it upon the seat. I have zero patience for young ladies who lack tidiness.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0001 }

“My mind was in such a state of distress yesterday evening that my clothing never crossed my thoughts,” said Nell. “I will tuck them away neatly this evening. At the asylum, we were perpetually forced to do so. Frequently, however, I would fail to remember, because I was so eager to slip into bed silently and indulge my imagination.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0002 }

“If you are going to remain here, remembering will need to be a bit easier for you,” Thirza warned. “Now, that appears more like it. Offer your prayers this instant and climb into bed.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0003 }

“I don’t ever pray,” Nell stated.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0004 }

Thirza appeared shock-stricken with horror.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0005 }

“Indeed, Nell, what is your meaning? Have you really not been instructed to offer your prayers? Young girls ought to pray, as God constantly desires it of them. Are you unaware of God’s identity, Nell?”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0006 }

“‘Being infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in His existence, wisdom, strength, holiness, justice, benevolence, and veracity, God is a spirit,’” Nell answered without delay or hesitation.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0007 }

Thirza appeared to be somewhat eased.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0008 }

“Thank goodness, you actually know a thing or two! You aren't entirely a pagan. How did you come to learn that?”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0009 }

“Oh, during Sunday-school at the asylum. Learning the entire catechism was required of us. I enjoyed it fairly well. A few of the words possess a magnificent quality. ‘Infinite, eternal and unchangeable.’ Is that not grand? It possesses a rolling sound—resembling a large organ being played. I imagine you could not precisely label it poetry, yet it possesses a very similar sound, does it not?”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0010 }

“We are discussing saying your prayers, Nell, rather than poetry. Are you unaware of what an awful, evil deed it is if you fail to say your prayers each evening? I fear that you are quite an awful little girl.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0011 }

“If your hair were red, being wicked would come more naturally to you than being good,” Nell remarked with blame in her voice. “The difficulties of life remain unknown to those without red hair. Mrs. Thomas informed me that my hair was made red by God intentionally, and my feelings for Him vanished after that. Besides, my exhaustion every evening would forever prevent me from troubling myself with prayers. Expecting folks who must care for twins to recite their prayers is unreasonable. Truly, is that not what you believe?”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0012 }

Thirza came to the conclusion that the initiation of Nell’s religious education required immediate action. Clearly, no time could be wasted.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0013 }

“As long as you live in my house, Nell, it is required that you say your prayers.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0014 }

“Why, naturally, provided that you wish it,” Nell agreed happily. “I would perform whatever needed doing to please you. However, you must instruct me on the words to speak for this single time. Once I am lying in bed, I am going to invent a truly lovely prayer that I can recite every time. Now that I reflect upon the matter, I think that it will prove to be rather entertaining.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0015 }

“It is necessary for you to kneel,” Thirza remarked awkwardly.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0016 }

Nell dropped to her knees beside Thirza and peered upward with a serious expression.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0017 }

“For what reason are individuals required to drop to their knees to offer prayers? Were I truly desirous of praying, I will inform you of my exact course of action. I would venture forth entirely by myself into an immense open field or penetrate the thickest, darkest forest, whereupon I would gaze upward toward the heavens—higher and higher—targeting that exquisite azure expanse that appears as though its color possesses no final boundary. Subsequently, I would simply experience a prayer within myself. Now then, I am prepared. Which words ought I to utter?”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0018 }

Thirza experienced an even greater sense of embarrassment. Her intention had been to instruct Nell in the juvenile classic, “Now I lay me down to sleep.” However, as I have recounted to you, she possessed the beginnings of a sense of humor—a quality that merely serves as another label for recognizing what is appropriate; and the realization abruptly struck her that the modest little prayer, held sacred by white-clad children lisping beside motherly knees, was wholly inappropriate for this freckled witch of a girl who possessed neither knowledge of nor concern for the love of God, given that human affection had never served to translate it to her.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0019 }

“Nell, your age is sufficient for you to offer your own prayers,” she eventually remarked. “Simply express gratitude to God for what He has bestowed upon you, and modestly request from Him the items you desire.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0020 }

“Well, I’ll do my best,” Nell assured her, pressing her face against the lap of Thirza. “Gracious heavenly Father—ministers use those words in church, which makes me think they’re appropriate for private prayer, doesn’t it?” she inserted, raising her head briefly. “Gracious heavenly Father, I thank Thee for the Petal Road of Delight and the Lake of Glassy Waters and Bonny and the Frost Maiden. I’m truly very thankful for those things. That covers every blessing I am able to recall at this moment to give thanks for. Regarding my desires, there are so many that listing every one would require a lot of time, which is why I’ll name just the two highest priorities. Please allow me to remain at Grey Shutters; and please allow me to turn out attractive as an adult. I remain,
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0021 }

“With respect, Nell Harcourt.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0022 }

“There, was my performance okay?” she inquired with enthusiasm, standing. “Had I been given slightly more time to consider it, I could have rendered it far more elaborate.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0023 }

Only the recollection that Nell’s astonishing prayer stemmed from a lack of spiritual knowledge rather than disrespect saved poor Thirza from falling apart entirely. After tucking the youngster into bed and inwardly resolving to instruct her in a prayer on the following day, she was departing from the chamber holding the lamp when Nell summoned her to return.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0024 }

“It has only just occurred to me. In lieu of ‘yours respectfully,’ I ought to have uttered ‘Amen,’ ought I not?—as ministers are accustomed to do. Though it had slipped my mind, I believed a prayer required a proper conclusion, which led me to include the former phrase. Is it your opinion that this will alter the outcome?”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0025 }

“I—I do not think it is likely to,” Thirza stated. “Now go off to sleep as a good child should. Good night.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0026 }

“Tonight, I am able to bid good night with an untroubled conscience,” Nell said, snuggling comfortably into her pillows.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0027 }

Withdrawing to the kitchen, Thirza placed the candle solidly upon the table and stared angrily at Obed.
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0028 }

“Obed Abernethy, that young girl ought to have been taken in by someone and given an education long ago. She is almost a complete pagan. Would you credit the fact that she had not uttered a single prayer her entire life until this evening? Tomorrow, I intend to request the loan of the Peep of the Day series from the manse, that is my plan. Furthermore, she will be sent to Sunday-school the moment I am able to sew appropriate garments for her. It is obvious to me that I will be kept very busy. Ah well, nobody passes through this life without enduring their portion of difficulty. My existence has been fairly comfortable up to this point, but my turn has finally arrived, and I imagine I must simply endure it as well as I can.”
{: #nw-v01-c07-p0029 }
